nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and vertices $i$ and $j$, adding the edge from $i$ to $j$ gives the adjacency matrix that has an edge from $i$ to $j$ and agrees with $m$ on every other ordered pair of vertices.
nodes.title: Edge insertion in an adjacency matrix

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, an adjacency matrix on $n$ vertices is a directed graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ given by a Boolean-valued function $\mathrm{adj}$ on ordered pairs of vertices: $\mathrm{adj}(i, j)$ is true exactly when there is a directed edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: Adjacency matrix

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the empty adjacency matrix on $n$ vertices is the directed graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with no edges: its adjacency function is false on every ordered pair of vertices.
nodes.title: Empty adjacency matrix

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and vertices $i$ and $j$, removing the edge from $i$ to $j$ gives the adjacency matrix that has no edge from $i$ to $j$ and agrees with $m$ on every other ordered pair of vertices.
nodes.title: Edge deletion in an adjacency matrix

nodes.summary: Two adjacency matrices $m$ and $m'$ on the same $n$ vertices are equal if, for all vertices $i$ and $j$, $m$ has an edge from $i$ to $j$ exactly when $m'$ does.
nodes.title: Extensionality of adjacency matrices

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on $n$ vertices and vertices $i$, $j$, $a$, $b$, the matrix obtained from $m$ by adding the edge from $i$ to $j$ has an edge from $a$ to $b$ if and only if $a = i$ and $b = j$, or $m$ has an edge from $a$ to $b$.
nodes.title: Edges after inserting an edge

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on $n$ vertices and vertices $i$, $j$, $a$, $b$ with $a \ne i$ or $b \ne j$, the matrix obtained from $m$ by adding the edge from $i$ to $j$ has an edge from $a$ to $b$ if and only if $m$ does.
nodes.title: Inserting an edge leaves other pairs unchanged

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on $n$ vertices and vertices $i$ and $j$, the matrix obtained from $m$ by adding the edge from $i$ to $j$ has an edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: An inserted edge is present

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and all vertices $i$ and $j$ among the $n$ vertices, the empty adjacency matrix on $n$ vertices has no edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: The empty adjacency matrix has no edges

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on $n$ vertices and vertices $i$, $j$, $a$, $b$, the matrix obtained from $m$ by removing the edge from $i$ to $j$ has an edge from $a$ to $b$ if and only if $(a, b) \ne (i, j)$ and $m$ has an edge from $a$ to $b$.
nodes.title: Edges after deleting an edge

nodes.summary:
Let $m$ be an adjacency matrix on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j, a, b$ be vertices with $(a, b) 
e (i, j)$, that is, $a 
e i$ or $b 
e j$. Then the graph obtained from $m$ by deleting the edge from $i$ to $j$ has an edge from $a$ to $b$ if and only if $m$ has an edge from $a$ to $b$.
nodes.title: Deleting an edge leaves the other entries unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an adjacency matrix on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j$ be vertices. Then the graph obtained from $m$ by deleting the edge from $i$ to $j$ has no edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: Deleting an edge removes it

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and vertices $i, j$, the edge query of $m$ at $(i, j)$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when $m$ has a directed edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: Edge query of an adjacency matrix

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an adjacency matrix on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j, b$ be vertices. Then $b$ belongs to the out-neighbor list of $i$ in the graph obtained from $m$ by adding the edge from $i$ to $j$ if and only if $b = j$ or $b$ belongs to the out-neighbor list of $i$ in $m$.
nodes.title: Out-neighbors after adding an edge

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an adjacency matrix on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j$ be vertices. Then $j$ belongs to the out-neighbor list of $i$ in the graph obtained from $m$ by adding the edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: Adding an edge makes its target an out-neighbor

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an adjacency matrix on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j$ be vertices. Then $j$ belongs to the out-neighbor list of $i$ if and only if $m$ has a directed edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: The out-neighbor list matches the edge query

nodes.summary: In the graph with no edges on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the out-neighbor list of every vertex $i$ is the empty list.
nodes.title: Out-neighbor lists of the empty graph

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a vertex $i$, no vertex occurs twice in the out-neighbor list of $i$.
nodes.title: Out-neighbor lists have no duplicates

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a vertex $i$, the out-neighbor list of $i$ is strictly increasing: every vertex in it is smaller than every vertex that comes after it.
nodes.title: Out-neighbor lists are strictly increasing

nodes.summary: For an adjacency matrix $m$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a vertex $i$, the out-neighbor list of $i$ is the list of all vertices $j$ such that $m$ has a directed edge from $i$ to $j$, in increasing order.
nodes.title: Out-neighbor list

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, given by its adjacency matrix, and let $i$ and $j$ be vertices. After the edge from $i$ to $j$ is deleted from $G$ (whether or not $G$ had that edge), $j$ is not an out-neighbor of $i$.
nodes.title: Deleting an edge removes the out-neighbor

nodes.summary: For every $n$, every vertex of the empty directed graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ has out-degree $0$.
nodes.title: Vertices of the empty graph have out-degree zero

nodes.summary: The out-degree of a vertex $i$ of a directed graph given by an adjacency matrix is the number of its out-neighbors, that is, the number of vertices $j$ such that there is an edge from $i$ to $j$.
nodes.title: Out-degree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
